review.alternative: Simple summary statistics might suffice if temporal granularity is irrelevant.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that summary metrics outperform functional mixed-effect models in anomaly detection.

claims.statement: Statistical frameworks and rigorous trial-by-trial analysis provide necessary foundations for detecting latent anomalies in complex temporal data and agent trajectories.

support.explanation: Demonstrates the importance of rigorous statistical frameworks over summary statistics to capture nuanced temporal behavior, applicable to detecting reasoning anomalies.
support.passage: study presents a statistical framework for the analysis of photometry signals and provides an open-source implementation. The evidence supporting the benefits of the presented functional mixed-effect modeling analysis as opposed to (1) summary statistics and (2) other pointwise regression models is convincing with a thorough comparison with other methods and datasets.

actions.findings: Statistical frameworks and rigorous trial-by-trial analysis provide necessary foundations for detecting latent anomalies in complex temporal data and agent trajectories. [source-c1015474a2724e05]
actions.limitations: Limited by reliance on general statistical models and high-level architectural proposals without direct empirical execution traces.
actions.next_questions: How can empirical error detection be standardized across heterogeneous agent trajectories?
actions.reason: Revised notebook incorporating substantive evidence from eLife and ACL findings.
actions.summary: Detecting reasoning blind spots requires rigorous frameworks that integrate statistical time-series analysis and structured goal-identity configurations to bound model confabulations.
actions.title: Unrecognized Reasoning Limits and Automated Error Detection
